hardness_rationale: *** FIELD VISIBILITY CONTRACT — read this first. AGENT-FACING: one_line_ask, client_brief, brand_identity_additions.{price_range, positioning, demographics, competitive_set}, the inputs as files, and deliverables stated as outcomes. GRADER-FACING ONLY, and never to be rendered into any agent prompt: brand_identity_additions.design_implication, stages[] in full (including decision_the_agent_must_make, subtasks and connector_tools), inputs[].gen_prompt and inputs[].realism_notes, traps, failure_gates, verifiers_auto, verifiers_human, element_reuse, options_required, this field, and connector_doability_note. The agent-facing fields carry goals, symptoms and commercial facts; they name no tool, no failure mode, no type classification, no call-to-action verb and no correction. The primary failure gate is a triage whose consequence is deliberately deferred by four stages. In S1 the agent commits to a per-piece preparation route across six superficially identical sweep frames, and the two pieces whose geometry defeats automatic subject isolation — a filigree pendant with eleven enclosed apertures that fill with captured sweep, and a pair of fully separated jhumka drops of which single-blob subject detection keeps one — return success and look entirely correct on the white store tiles, because pale fill on a white ground is invisible. The defect first becomes visible in S5, on the campaign's colour field, and again in S6 on the deck's dark cover. Correcting it requires the agent to know that a background removal cannot open an enclosed hole no matter what ground colour it is given, that the working route is a positive selection of the piece by its own form and material, inverted, then a masked solid fill in PNG — which fills the outer ground and the apertures with the same exact value in one pass — and that the value to fill with is the panel colour it has not yet chosen. That is what makes S1, S4 and S5 genuinely dependent rather than merely sequential, and the chroma floor in VA-09 closes the shortcut of choosing a near-neutral panel so the agreement check passes trivially while hiding everything. Two things make it hard for a skilled human as well. Cross-asset consistency to a target: six frames shot across two afternoons in moving light with declared deltas (two warm, one cool, one a stop under, one rotated 2.4 degrees, one on reference), corrected individually by eye toward one silver white point against a physical step wedge, where one global setting or a per-frame automatic pass visibly fails to match — and where VA-18 requires the applied parameters to be directionally consistent with each frame's actual condition, not merely different from one another. And constraint-reasoning around tool limitations stacked four deep on the mark: it must be reached at marking level rather than object level, reached per element because a compound lockup comes back partial, traced in the correct polarity, and then cleaned of an opaque backing path and given a coordinate system it does not ship with — plus a reversed colourway the deck cover needs and nothing produces automatically. Every one of those five defects is invisible against white and fatal on a dark ground six steps later. The strategic trap is the price band, and it is now genuinely a derivation rather than a transcription: nothing agent-facing names a correction, a type classification or a CTA register. The founder reports only symptoms (people ask about payment plans; they are surprised when they reach a number) and hands over facts (890 to 4,900, a 2,850 average order, a published three-piece bundle carrying a real 600-rupee saving, a phone-first payday buyer, three ad slots of which two are mobile). An agent that follows the type recommender's fine-jewellery drawer produces a technically flawless look ten times the brand's price: hairline display serifs that die in a 640x100 banner, one piece per frame instead of the set the modal order is built on, and no price on a brand whose entire diagnosed problem is that shoppers assume it is out of reach. VH-01 measures that blind against a fixed, supplied control fixture built once and reused. Acceptance does not require the agent to measure anything and no verifier depends on it having done so. The grader checks exact artboard counts and pixel dimensions on five documents, a photographic element census that catches a silently dropped background nothing else can see, viewBox present and no full-bleed backing path plus three colourways on the mark, no upscale factor anywhere in the run, step-wedge neutrality within 8 levels and cross-frame agreement within 10 on the retained masters with wedge-exclusion checked separately on the delivered crops, a non-neutral declared panel whose value string-matches every panel-matched plate, catalogue prices and wholesale figures consistent across fifteen surfaces with the bundle saving recomputed and required to be shown, a pinned price display convention graded separately from the arithmetic, a byte-identical destination on every customer-facing surface with a decodable code on the poster and the tag, at least two pieces composed together on the poster, the feed square and an ad unit with three together somewhere, a price at or above a stated proportional size on every campaign artboard, a size-and-weight floor on every text element in the ad units that fails hairline faces automatically, six pages for six rows with four bound fields and two fixed lines, 650x1004 at 300 dpi on the proofs, and a six-entry treatment sheet whose parameters agree in sign with each frame's declared condition. Length is managed rather than pretended away: the six store tiles are one recipe run six times and are explicitly NOT counted as difficulty, the multi-image tools are batched at their ceiling, the two prose-heavy tools are called once each per role, and the stage plan is cut into four resumable checkpoints (S1-S3, S4-S5, S6-S7, S8) so that a stamina failure is distinguishable from a design failure and a rerun does not restart from intake.
why_not_a_vlm_one_shot: A chat model with an image generator can describe this campaign and can render a picture of it; it cannot produce it. Nothing in a one-shot generator licenses a camera-scale material surface and records the licence and the AI-generated flag against it, neutralises six differently-lit frames toward a shared white point and reports six parameter sets whose signs agree with each frame's actual condition, recovers a lost logo from a photograph of a letterpress proof into a scalable vector assembled from per-element traces with its counters open and its backing plate removed and a reversed colourway derived from it, binds four catalogue fields into a six-page press file from last year's flat PDF at 300 dpi, or lands any of it as native editable documents in the client's own account with live licensed type in the correct family and weight, real table structure and drawn vector charts. The client's editability rule is not a preference, it is the commercial reason she is hiring: she has been burned by flat pictures she had to pay to change and asked explicitly for files she can open and edit when a price moves, and the handover is graded on whether a price actually can be changed and still resolve to the licensed face afterwards. A rendered image of a poster fails the brief on its face however good it looks. Beyond production, the reasoning is not one-shot. The preparation route chosen in Stage 1 is only vindicated or destroyed by a panel value chosen in Stage 4 and a composition built in Stage 5. The recovered mark carries five latent defects — wrong source capture, substrate instead of marking, a partial compound lift, wrong polarity, an unstripped backing path with no coordinate system — every one of which is invisible against white and only surfaces on a dark cover six steps later. The type system has to survive simultaneously at A3 and inside a 320x50 mobile banner, and the tool that recommends type explicitly refuses to pair faces or to warn about either constraint. And every intermediate step in the chain reports success regardless of what it silently dropped, so a single-pass generator has no mechanism to discover any of it. The engagement is graded on twenty-five placements of one recovered element across fifteen surfaces staying consistent, on arithmetic matching a supplied catalogue including a bundle saving that must be shown as well as computed, on a destination string being byte-identical everywhere and a code that actually decodes, on six pages matching six rows with four bound fields, and on a strategy argument derived — not transcribed — from an 890-to-4,900 band and a 2,850 order. None of that is a picture, and none of it a one-shot describes into existence.
connector_doability_note: Every deliverable maps to a chain verified in the current live capability audit; nothing draws on a banned or unreachable capability, and three items are flagged below as pre-ship pilots rather than assumed. ACCOUNT/INPUTS: account_type is "auth"; all client files reach the tools headlessly via asset_initialize_file_upload then a curl PUT then asset_finalize_file_upload — no file picker, no widget. STUDIO PASS, WITH THE OPERATION ORDER PINNED: image_apply_adjustments per frame for exposure, temperature, tint, contrast, highlights and shadows (never image_apply_auto_tone, never one global setting); image_auto_straighten for sku_04, applied BEFORE any isolation because the crop bounds derive from it; then per-piece preparation; then image_crop_to_bounds using padded bounds taken from the selection's returnBbox; then image_crop_and_resize DOWN to 1600x1600 LAST, asserting metadata.upscale_factor equals 1 and an empty or downscale-only tradeoffs array at every step. Sources are declared at 4096x3072 with each piece occupying at least 60% of the 3072px short edge, so a padded square crop stays comfortably above 1600px even after background removal's silent downscale of an oversized input — which is the specific path by which a naive final resize would otherwise take the free 2x interpolation VA-05 forbids. PER-PIECE PREPARATION, TWO ROUTES: safe pieces (ST-01, SB-02, CB-03, OC-06) go through image_remove_background to transparent RGBA PNG, whose alpha is verified to survive both crop tools at outputFileType png. The two trap pieces (FP-04, JE-05) go through image_select_by_prompt naming the piece by its own form and material, then image_invert_selection, then image_fill_area with the locked panel value at outputFileType png — this fills the outer ground AND the enclosed apertures with the same exact value in one pass, yields PNG rather than the JPEG a backgroundColor knockout returns (so no compression fringe around high-contrast silver), and makes VA-09's exact-string gate meaningful. image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) is retained as the NAIVE path that trips the trap, never as the prescribed route: it isolates the outer background only and cannot punch an enclosed hole. outputFileType png is held through the entire selection, fill and crop chain — a single jpeg step destroys mask and alpha fidelity downstream. PRE-SHIP PILOT 1: run the FP-04 openwork route live once (positive selection naming the piece by material and form, invert, fill_area) and confirm the apertures land in the inverted mask, since the verified evidence for enclosed-counter exclusion comes from a printed graphic rather than from an openwork object. If the mask comes back as a filled silhouette, fall back to per-element selection composited and demote the pendant, leaving JE-05's disjoint-component trap as the sole isolation gate — the multi-instance behaviour behind JE-05 is directly verified. MARK RECOVERY: image_select_by_prompt reaches marking level on a coloured-ink impression (verified stroke-accurate with counters excluded); each lockup element is selected separately because a single selection over a compound mark is verified to come back unreliably partial; image_invert_selection sets polarity; image_crop_to_bounds from the selection's returned bounds; image_vectorize traces. The missing viewBox and the leading full-canvas backing path are both documented behaviours and are fixed locally before the SVG is inlined. Colourways are authored locally off the master. capture_02 (debossed same-metal tag) is a declared decoy and no stage or verifier requires marking-level isolation from it. AUTHORED LAYOUTS: the directions document, poster, social set, ad set and deck are authored as self-contained fixed-canvas HTML through create_visual_design_express_skill then html_export_readiness_skill then export_html_to_express — fully headless, synchronous, returning native editable Express documents. Multi-artboard in one call is verified, as are mixed canvas sizes inside one document (exactly what the five-format social set and the three-unit ad set require), absolute-unit print canvases (297x420mm resolving at 96dpi to 1123x1587px), real editable text with mixed-weight inline runs, live tables with per-cell fills and strokes (the deck's price and terms tables), inline SVG converting to native editable vector paths (the rollout chart, the recovered mark, the scannable code), gradients, radius, rotation, single shadows and circular photo crops. hz:slide-selector names the PER-ARTBOARD class, never the wrapper, and canvasWidth/canvasHeight/slideSelector are NEVER passed as tool parameters — both mistakes silently destroy a mixed-size set. PRE-SHIP PILOT 2: the ad units are authored at 2x their display size (600x500, 640x100, 600x1200) precisely because every canvas in the audit is 1000px or larger on the short edge and no minimum-canvas behaviour is established; 2x authoring is standard retina ad practice, keeps the aspect ratios exact, and removes the untested-small-root risk from VA-01. Confirm a 640x100 root round-trips before shipping; if it normalises, raise the banner to 960x150 at the same ratio and restate the display size. TYPOGRAPHY: font_recommend once per role and no more (each response carries a roughly 4KB prose instruction blob), font_styles for the family-specific numeric weights (mandatory — the numbers are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from style names), find_fonts to launder every name into canonical PostScript form before any embed request, then a single get_fontkit_embed_url covering the whole campaign. One unlaundered or wrongly-cased name kills the entire kit, so laundering is not optional. Families are addressed in CSS by the returned css_stack slug, never by the PostScript name, and font-family AND font-weight are declared on every text element rather than on body alone. The returned Typekit link is the one external stylesheet the importer permits, so the licensed faces survive into Express as live text. suggest_type_palettes and get_type_palette are not surfaced and are not designed against. IMAGERY INTO LAYOUT: every photograph is base64-embedded in an element — never referenced by URL (silently substituted with a transparent placeholder that keeps the element's geometry) and never carried in a CSS background (dropped entirely, leaving no element to detect). PRE-SHIP PILOT 3 and the transport rule: prove the hosted route ONCE and early — upload a trivial HTML through asset_initialize/finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html and export it by url, confirming slide_count — before committing five photo-bearing documents to it, since every verified export in the audit was inline. Inline fallback is specified rather than left to chance: downscale every embedded photograph to the size it is actually rendered at, prefer inline SVG markup over base64 (roughly 25% smaller), and treat the 70KB threshold as an advisory the studio states rather than a gate it stalls on. STOCK: asset_search with entityScope StockAsset using SHORT queries and no orientation filter (that filter returns zero hits), candidate screening done by fetching the public 240px renditionURL locally and viewing it as a local file, then asset_license_and_download_stock for the two or three that survive — fully headless, genuine full-resolution photography, with isGenTech exposed so AI-generated assets are excluded. No-people screening is an agent judgement recorded per asset in the licensing record and graded human-side, because no tool exposes a people flag. BOARDS: boards_create_new_board plus boards_add_items_to_board (both persistent and headless; create_firefly_board is a URL builder and is not used), five to eight placements in one call, raster only, unlicensed reference thumbnails permitted and labelled. HANGTAG RUN: convert_pdf_to_indd on a declared genuine font-embedding print export containing a placed raster (the only thing that yields a mappable graphic frame), then export_idml, then generate_indd_mapping_prompt ONCE plus one validation call, then the mandatory extra step the tools do not prompt for — download and unzip the IDML and reconstruct each frame's true story text from its own content runs, computing every offset from that rather than from the tool's lossy textContent — then prepare_indd_merge_template with the whole mapping as a single JSON string, then export_idml again to CONFIRM every placeholder actually landed, then document_merge_data_layout to one multi-page PDF (one record per page, page count equals row count, order verified correct for PDF), then document_render_layout at resolution 300 for the proofs (the merge step's own resolution parameter is silently ignored). The recovered stamp is rasterised locally to a transparent PNG at 55x85mm-at-300dpi scale and placed as a STATIC image via image_mappings action replace_all — legitimate for images, forbidden for text — because a vector cannot be bound as a merge image and the mark is identical on all six cards. Fallback if export_idml shows zero graphic frames: drop the mark from the merge and declare the omission rather than fail the stage. No bleed and no named press preset are asked for, since neither is obtainable from a PDF-derived template and pdfPreset is a closed undiscoverable enum. The scannable code is produced locally as an inline SVG module matrix (poster) and a transparent PNG (hangtag) — no connector tool generates one, and the connector's documented variable per-record code is inert, which is exactly why the spec requires ONE static store link on all six cards. SELF-VERIFICATION, SCOPED HONESTLY: asset_inline_preview on each prepared piece's own presigned URL is where the pixel-level halo, aperture and missing-component checks happen, upstream, where they are fully doable. In-layout checking is artboard 1 by rendition preview (asset_search then asset_get_presigned_urls then asset_inline_preview) and artboards 2..N by parsing the returned slides[].html — which catches placeholder payloads, off-canvas coordinates, collapsed widths and wrong resolved typefaces but not halos — with a throwaway single-root export sanctioned where a genuine visual check is unavoidable. Whole-layout pixel judgement is left to the human verifiers. BUDGET: one font_recommend per role, one mapping-prompt call plus one validation, multi-image tools batched at their 10-image ceiling and never above it, and note the routing doc's roughly 20-file ceiling is per operation rather than per engagement, so the roughly 25 files this run touches are fine. EXPLICITLY AVOIDED: no text-to-image, no generative fill, no AI object removal, no background-replace-by-prompt, no compositing of two photographs (sets are built by arranging prepared per-piece assets at coordinates over a licensed surface in the authored layout), no cartoonize, no upscaling anywhere, no OCR, no measurement asked of the agent, no image_generative_expand anywhere in the run (deleted from every stage — every target crop is a downscale from a 4096x3072 or 7360x4912 source, which is what keeps VA-05 unambiguous), no template gallery or human pick (search_design, fill_text and replace_image are unused; fill_text is non-deterministic and lossy), no animate_design (returns no artifact), no video or audio family (async with no reachable poll tool in this host), no variable per-record code, no per-artboard file export, and no export of a file out of the Express documents — download_design is not surfaced, which is why the poster is correctly specified as the editable artboard the client's own print shop pulls from her account, and why the only 300 DPI claim in the engagement sits on the InDesign render where it is verified.

engagement_title: Azura Cliff go-to-market kit: recovered crest, house grade, three routes and the full launch collateral suite
one_line_ask: Take one cliffside villa from three unusable photographs, a lost monogram and a flat legacy PDF to a complete launch kit — recovered artwork, an authored type system, a graded set of imagery, three defended art directions, the finished poster, social set, particulars document, ad units and listing imagery, and the printed viewing cards for the broker preview.

brand_identity_additions.price_range: Azura Cliff freehold guide €4.6M–€5.2M, never published — 'price on request', said out loud. Out of season the house is let privately at €4,200–€7,500 per night, seven-night minimum. The wider Coralline portfolio runs €2.8M–€9M across eleven coastal villas; roughly three sales close per year.
brand_identity_additions.positioning: A five-person private brokerage, not a portal. One asset marketed at a time, slowly, to a hand-built list of brokers and known clients. The collateral's job is to earn a viewing and to be the second time a buyer has seen the name — never to close anyone.
brand_identity_additions.demographics: Buyers 45–65, second or third home, household investable assets €15M+, cash or private-bank lending, reached through brokers and word of mouth rather than search. Decision cycle 6–18 months with two or three site visits; no impulse conversion exists in this funnel. The private-hire audience is a different person entirely — a 6–12 person extended family or a small executive retreat, booking 4–9 months ahead, choosing between three or four houses on the same coast, and reading the same brand at a materially lower commitment.
brand_identity_additions.design_implication: The €4.6M–€5.2M band decides the layout, and it must be visible in the artefacts: no price, no 'from', no rate, no countdown, no offer flash, no button-shaped CTA on any canvas; the response mechanism is the office line and the particulars notice set quietly inside the margin, never in a box. One photograph per canvas (the single honest-view page of the particulars document is the one exception). Text and the crest hold at or outside 8% of the short edge on the poster, the particulars pages and the social roots — photography may bleed to the trim, and does not count against that margin. Type set small relative to the canvas with generous leading; a high-contrast display face reserved for the name line and one quiet text face for everything else; the crest placed small, as a mark of provenance, never scaled up as a logo slap. THESE RULES GOVERN THE DELIVERED SUITE ONLY — the three exploratory route comps are bound only by the non-negotiables (no price, no rate, no CTA, true representation, agency line and notice present) and are free, indeed required, to vary margin, crest scale and role, image treatment and typographic hierarchy; the recommendation must then argue the chosen route back to these rules. The ad units carry the intent but not the percentages: on a 300×250 and a 728×90 the discipline is expressed as legibility floors (mark and name line above a stated minimum at 1:1, a stated minimum edge clearance) rather than an 8% margin, which at that size would guarantee the failure the unit exists to avoid. Invert the band to a €180–€320-a-night short-let and every one of those decisions should visibly flip — rate badge on every frame, four-up collage, saturated grade, heavy sans, a 'Book now' bar, seasonal flash, tight margins. A grader comparing the delivered suite against that counterfactual should be able to tell which band it was made for without being told. The hire band is not decoration: the agent must decide, and argue, whether the €4,200–€7,500 audience sees the same set or a variant of it, and produce the variant if it argues for one.
brand_identity_additions.competitive_set: Other single-asset cliffside listings marketed by small private brokerages; boutique villa-collection operators letting the same class of house nightly. Not portals, not volume agencies.

client_brief:
Hello — I handle marketing for Coralline Estates. There are five of us. We hold eleven villas along this stretch of coast and we close about three sales a year, so there is no volume to hide behind: every listing has to carry itself completely, on its own.

Azura Cliff comes to market on the 3rd of next month and I need the whole launch kit from you, not pieces of it.

Before you design anything, the thing that decides almost everything. The guide is €4.6M–€5.2M, and out of season we let the house privately at €4,200–€7,500 a night with a seven-night minimum. Our buyers are between forty-five and sixty-five, this is their second or third house, they pay cash or through a private bank, and they take somewhere between six and eighteen months and two or three visits before they decide. Nobody has ever seen a piece of paper from us and bought a house. So: we do not print the price, ever. No "from", no "starting at", no countdown, no seasonal offer, no discount, and nothing that looks like a shopping button. Price is on request and it gets said out loud, one person to one person. If our collateral looks like it is trying to close someone, it does the opposite of what we need. I am telling you this at length because I have been sent beautiful work before that was pitched about three price bands below us and it was unusable.

The hire side is a genuinely different person — a family of ten, or a small board, booking half a year out, choosing between three or four houses on this coast. I do not want two identities and I am not asking for a second brand. But I would like you to tell me whether that audience sees exactly the same set or a variant of it, and if you think there should be a variant, show me it rather than describing it.

What you have to work with.

Three photographs, capture_01 to capture_03, straight off the photographer's card and converted, about 4800 px on the long edge — an interior with the sea through it, the pool deck, and the terrace. He shot across one day and then he was gone, so this is all there is. Side by side they look like three different houses in three different countries, which is exactly the problem, because half of what I am asking you for puts them side by side. They need to look like one house, one day, one hand behind the camera. Send me the corrected full frames as well as the crops — we archive every shoot at full size exactly as corrected, and I file those the day they arrive. And on anything published: nothing in the frame that is not the house. His kit, his assistant's bits and pieces, a stray reflection — if it is not part of what a buyer walks into, it does not go out.

One rule from our compliance side that I cannot bend. Everything we publish about this property has to be a true representation of what a buyer will actually walk into. Nothing invented, nothing added, nothing extended, nothing that was not in the room when the shutter went. That is about the property specifically. Atmosphere or landscape that is plainly not a picture of this house is a different matter and I am comfortable with you sourcing something appropriate and licensed — as long as it is real photography, honestly used, and it belongs to this coast. Same light, same water, same vegetation. A beautiful cliff from the wrong sea is a lie by implication and I will spot it.

The crest. We have a monogram — a coral-branch mark inside a ring with our name set around it. The studio that drew it closed two years ago and took the source files with them. What came off their drive when they folded are two captures, ref_01 and ref_02. Nobody here took them and I genuinely do not know what either of them is a photograph of. I need the mark back as real artwork, because it goes on every single thing in this kit: it sits on our deep ink ground, it goes in the corner of a small ad, and it goes on the poster in the sales-office window. It has to be right in all of those. And while you are in there — write me the rules for it. Minimum size, how much air it needs, which colourways are approved, what nobody is ever allowed to do to it. We lost this mark once. I would like the next person who touches it to have a page to follow.

Attached: our one-page brand sheet — Ink #10222B, Stone #E8E2D8, and one accent we call Coral, #C9563C, used sparingly or not at all. A copy deck with four headline options, the body paragraph, the spec bullets, our agency line, the office number and the particulars notice our compliance officer requires. A CSV of the floor areas and the room schedule. viewing_card.pdf and viewings.csv, which I will come to.

Run one of the four headlines. Tell me which and why — and if you think none of them are right, write me a better one and say so.

Everything that goes out in public carries our name, the office line and the particulars notice — small, set quietly, inside the margin, never in a box. That plus the house is all that goes on the poster. No price and nothing to press.

We have never had a typeface of our own. Please choose one, two at most, and make it a real licensed choice you can defend rather than whatever is lying around — and please actually set the work in it rather than describing it to me.

Here is what I need delivered.

A window poster for the sales office at A3, portrait, at true print size.

A social set for the launch — one square, one vertical story frame, one landscape — that reads as one family, not three separate posts.

The particulars document: five A4 pages, portrait. This is the thing we send ahead of a viewing and it is also the thing an assistant prints and puts in front of somebody, which is why it is A4 and not a widescreen slideshow — everybody in this market reads particulars on paper or as a portrait PDF on a phone. It opens on atmosphere, shows the house honestly, carries the spec table off the CSV, and closes on us rather than on a sell. One page of it has to deal with the floor areas: the architect's plan is being redrawn and I will not have it before the 3rd, so for now I need the areas shown as a quiet schedule — terrace against interior against pool deck — something set in our own type that sits with the rest of the document. Not a pie chart. When the plan arrives it replaces that page, so tell me that in writing.

A small set of digital ad units. We are booked into a private-client publication's network for six weeks; they take a 1200×628, a 300×250 and a 728×90 and nothing else. These are not there to be clicked and nobody will click them — they run so that when a broker says our name to a client, it is the second time that client has seen it. The 300×250 is the one I care about, because it is where our name has to be legible at actual size, and every version I have been sent so far has just been the poster shrunk.

Listing imagery for the property page: the main wide hero, three portrait gallery frames, and one vertical frame for a story link.

And the printer's problem — this one is first, not last. We are opening the house for two days to eight of the brokers on our list and two couples who have already been round once. Each of them gets a card at the door with their name on it, the date and their slot time, who is bringing them and that broker's direct line. Our print vendor will only accept a proper InDesign file, and all that exists is viewing_card.pdf, which the old studio exported before they folded. The card design itself is fine and should stay exactly as it is — it just has to become something that can be run against the roster, which is viewings.csv. I need the InDesign file for the vendor, the press file with every guest on their own page, and each guest's card as its own file named to them, because our office manager hands them out individually.

Two things about how I want to receive this.

First: do not send me one idea. Send me three genuinely different directions for how this campaign looks and reads — different enough that I could not turn one into another by changing a colour — and show them to me as three A3 posters at real size, because that is the piece that carries the campaign and a small square tells me nothing about how the type sits or how small the crest wants to be. Then tell me which one you would run and why, in terms of who is actually buying this house. I am in the mountains with the family until the 28th and there is no time to send this back and forth, so build the whole thing to the route you pick and make the argument in writing. If I disagree when I land we will change one thing, not six. That is why the fee is what it is and why I am asking for the reasoning rather than a presentation.

Second: we have Express seats here and my office manager exports whatever you build, so send me the built documents — live, editable, in the real typeface — not flattened pictures. We re-time the social posts ourselves and I edit the particulars between viewings, so I need to be able to open these and change a line without coming back to you. What I do need alongside them is a one-page handover telling her exactly what to export from each document, at what size, and where it goes — the printer, the network, the property page, the posts. And do not hand me a folder of files with no reasoning attached: tell me what you did to the photographs and why each one needed something different, why the type is the type, what the crest turned out to be and what you had to do to make it usable, and be straight with me about anything you could not check or could not produce. The files are half of it. The judgement is the other half and it is the half I am actually paying for.

Fee is €11,500, half on the 22nd and half on delivery. The dates behind it: the card file has to be with the vendor by the 22nd because they close for stocktake and then need three working days; the poster has to be with the printer by the 26th; the particulars and the listing imagery I need in my hands on the 1st; we launch on the 3rd.

— Ilaria Vasse, Coralline Estates

stages.name: Stage 1 — Neutralise and rectify: the three archive masters
stages.goal: Take capture_01/02/03 — shot at three times of day, one of them with a visibly tilted sea horizon — and produce three full-frame corrected masters that are neutral, geometrically correct and mutually consistent, retained at full size as the client's archive.
stages.decision_the_agent_must_make: To look at all three before touching any of them, and to converge them by dialing divergent per-frame corrections rather than applying auto-tone or one identical parameter set. Auto-tone succeeds on every call and yields three individually plausible, collectively incoherent frames; the incoherence exists only between the frames and is invisible until Stage 7 puts three of them on one page. The agent must also notice on its own that one frame is not level, recognise that tone tools cannot rotate and that exactly one operation rectifies a tilt, and understand that rectification has to precede every crop or every derived output inherits the tilt. Nothing in the brief says which frame, or in which direction any frame is wrong.
subtasks: Upload the three captures headlessly and inspect each one before choosing any parameter.
Find and rectify the geometric fault before any tonal work and before any crop is committed.
Neutralise each frame by eye against what is in shot, then converge all three on a common white point, black point and warmth using per-frame divergent settings.
Export the three corrected full frames, unchanged in framing, as the client's archive masters.
Write the applied-settings log: per frame, the parameters dialed and the reason that frame needed different numbers from the other two. Report settings applied, never values read.
stages.feeds_into: Stage 6 (the route grade is applied on top of these, and every listing crop derives from the graded masters) and Stage 7 (the poster, social set and particulars all place derivatives; a failed convergence surfaces on the honest-view page).

stages.name: Stage 2 — Recover the crest and make it genuinely usable
stages.goal: Get the coral-branch-in-a-ring monogram back as real, placeable artwork that sits on the deep ink ground with nothing behind it, holds as a corner mark on a 300×250 and as an element on an A3 sheet, and is governed by a usage note.
stages.decision_the_agent_must_make: Which of ref_01 and ref_02 is the artwork source. They are the same mark, the same file type, neutrally named, and both are flat captures of a printed card — one evenly lit, complete, slightly soft; the other shot in raking light on textured letterpress stock, apparently crisper and higher in contrast, but with abraded ink that has broken two stroke groups and a paper tooth that reads as ink under any selection. The tempting capture is the one that looks better on screen; tracing it succeeds and returns a mark with broken strokes and texture speckle that is invisible on a pale preview and ruinous at poster scale and on the ink ground. The agent must then decide how to name the selection — naming the substrate ('the crest on the card', 'the plaque') pulls the mask to the card and yields a rectangle, while naming the graphic's own colour, medium and line quality pulls it to the ink — decide polarity before tracing, recognise that no background-removal route can open the enclosed centre of a ring or hold a disjoint lettering ring, and finally decide what 'usable' means: the raw trace carries a full-canvas opaque backing path and no coordinate system, neither of which any tool repairs, and the full trace is far too many paths to hold at ad-corner size.
subtasks: Inspect both captures at magnification and choose the artwork source on the evidence in the pixels, not on the filename or first impression.
Isolate the mark at ink level and verify by looking at the mask, not by trusting the call's success.
Set polarity correctly before tracing, and tighten to the mark's own bounds.

Trace to vector, then perform the hygiene no tool performs: remove the opaque full-canvas backing path, inject a coordinate system so the mark scales, and confirm the ring centre and the letterform counters are genuinely open when composited over the brand ink.

Produce the derived treatments the kit needs from the same extraction: a reduced-path single-colour version for every placement below the stated small-scale threshold, a stone-on-ink and an ink-on-stone colourway, and a flat stone-ground raster for the print path — stated plainly as non-transparent, because no transparent knockout of this shape is producible.
Write the mark usage note: minimum reproduction width, clear space in units of the mark, approved colourways and grounds, and the forbidden uses.
Write the recovery note: what the crest turned out to be, which capture was usable and why, what the other one is good for, and what had to be repaired after tracing.
stages.feeds_into: Stages 4, 5 and 7 — one extraction is placed at five scales across the poster, three social roots, five particulars pages and three ad units, and is reconciled against the printed viewing card. A wrong source, an unrepaired trace or a full-path mark used at ad-corner size breaks all of them at once.

stages.name: Stage 3 — Author a type system the brand has never had
stages.goal: Choose and license a display face and a text face, establish how each is actually addressed and weighted, and make them live type in every authored document rather than a recommendation in a report.
stages.decision_the_agent_must_make: The pairing itself, which no tool will make — candidates come back per role and the agent must pick one display and one text face that sit at the €4.6M–€5.2M register and defend the pair against the buyer's decision cycle rather than against taste. It must also decide to verify how each family is really addressed before writing a line of CSS: the string that must appear in the CSS is not the PostScript name, numeric weights are not standardised across families so the reflexive value can silently render a Light cut, display cuts live under their own family slug rather than at a high weight, one unresolvable name destroys an entire embed including the valid faces, and the documented similarity fallback returns unrelated categories. Every one of those failures renders successfully and looks like a font.
subtasks: Brief the two typographic roles separately and read the candidate sets as art direction rather than as an answer.
Pick the pair and write the rationale against the price band and the decision cycle.
Establish the real per-style numeric weights and the real family addressing for both faces before authoring anything, laundering every name through the canonical lookup first.
Build one embed covering every face the whole kit uses and carry that single embed identically into all five authored documents.
Declare family and weight explicitly on every text element, and confirm from the imported document that the face that landed is the face that was chosen.
stages.feeds_into: Stages 5 and 7 — the same embed and the same weight decisions govern the route comps, the poster, the social set, the particulars document and the ad units, so a mis-addressed family is wrong ten times over and reads as a default sans throughout.

stages.name: Stage 4 — The printer's deadline: rebuild the viewing card and run the roster (front-loaded)
stages.goal: Turn viewing_card.pdf back into a working InDesign template with live fields, run it against the ten-guest broker-preview roster, and deliver the vendor's InDesign file, the press file and one named file per guest — all before the 22nd, ahead of any design work on the suite.
stages.decision_the_agent_must_make: Whether to trust the template's own reported contents. The converted document's field structure has to be established by inspecting the document itself rather than the summary the tooling offers: that summary drops a text run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset after the omission is wrong by a fixed amount. The validator then passes it, the placeholder step reports success, and two of the six fields silently never land — nothing surfaces until a merged card comes out with a blank line where the slot time should be. The agent must also decide the delivery mechanics: the press file and the per-guest files come off different routes, and one of the raster routes returns records in an order that contradicts its own labels, so it has to choose a route where record identity is guaranteed rather than inferred, and name the files itself because nothing else will. Finally it must decide what it cannot promise: a template that originates as a PDF carries no bleed and the press-preset enum is undiscoverable, so those must be reported rather than asserted.
subtasks: Convert the supplied press PDF and inspect the resulting document's real frame inventory and true story text before promising any mapping.

Compute the six-field mapping from the document's actual contents, validate it, then re-inspect the prepared template to confirm every field is genuinely present rather than trusting the success message.
Merge the ten-guest roster to a single press file, one guest per page.
Produce one file per guest, named to the guest, by a route where the record's identity is guaranteed.
Deliver the prepared InDesign template itself, which is what the vendor actually requires.
Confirm the card's crest and palette reconcile with the rest of the kit, and report what a PDF-sourced template cannot carry.
stages.feeds_into: The physical piece handed over at the door, and the identity reconciliation in Stage 8 — the printed card and the screen suite must read as one brand.

stages.name: Stage 5 — Three routes at real size, one licensed frame, and a defended pick
stages.goal: Give the client three genuinely different art directions presented as A3 posters at true size, source the one piece of imagery the shoot does not contain, and recommend a route with an argument grounded in who buys this house.
stages.decision_the_agent_must_make: What counts as a different direction rather than a variant. The comps are bound only by the non-negotiables — no price, no rate, no CTA, true representation, agency line and notice present — and are explicitly free to vary the register rules that govern the delivered suite. The agent must move at least three of four named axes across the three routes (image treatment and crop philosophy; grid and margin discipline; the crest's role and scale; typographic hierarchy and the size relationship between name line and body) and declare, per comp, which axes it moved and what that costs. Then the pick: argued from the €4.6M–€5.2M band and the 6–18 month cycle, argued back against the pinned register rules it will then have to obey, and actually executed in Stage 7. Separately it must decide what atmosphere imagery is legitimate: real photography, not machine-generated, plainly not a depiction of the house, regionally plausible against three frames of this coast, and brought down at working resolution rather than as the browsing thumbnail the search returns. It must also decide the hire-audience question and be able to show, not describe, whatever it concludes.
subtasks: Load the authoring skill, then author three A3 portrait comps as one exported document, each a real composition rather than a description of one.

Shortlist at least five candidate context frames, filter them on provenance, machine-generation and regional plausibility, license exactly one, and bring it down at full resolution through the local shell before re-uploading it for any further processing. Persist the shortlist as a board.
Render the exported document and inspect comp 1 visually; verify the other two roots from the returned per-slide structure, and state plainly which was confirmed how.

Write the recommendation: which route, why it is right for this band and this buyer, what the rejected two would have cost the brand, how the route sits with the register rules it now has to obey, and whether the hire audience gets the same set or a variant.
stages.feeds_into: Stage 6 (the route dictates the grade) and Stage 7 (the route is the specification the whole suite is built to). A route picked and not executed is a visible inconsistency across six deliverables.

stages.name: Stage 6 — Apply the route grade and cut the listing imagery
stages.goal: Put an authored, declared look on top of the neutral masters in service of the chosen route, then deliver the wide hero, three portrait gallery frames and one vertical story frame from those graded masters.
stages.decision_the_agent_must_make: First, the look itself: the agent states the grade it is authoring — where the black point sits, how the shadows are held, how far the highlights roll off, how much warmth the route wants — and then reaches it with divergent per-frame parameters so the three frames agree on the new, non-neutral target rather than on neutral. A grade that is merely 'corrected' is a technical fix, not an art direction, and it must be recognisably the route the agent just recommended. Second, derivation: cutting the wide hero and then re-cutting the portrait and vertical formats out of that hero is the tempting path, and the vertical in particular then has to be enlarged back up, which happens silently and is disclosed only in a field that is easy to skip. Every format is cut independently from the full graded master. Third, the compliance decision: a vertical frame from a landscape interior will not fill without either a much tighter crop or manufactured content, and the true-representation rule makes the tighter crop the only acceptable answer for property imagery — the tooling will actively offer the canvas-extension chain as the tidy fix. Fourth, everything foreign to the house must be framed out of all six delivered crops while the archive masters keep their full framing.
subtasks: Declare the route grade in words before applying it, then reach it on all three frames with divergent per-frame parameters.
Cut the wide hero, three portrait gallery frames and the vertical story frame, each independently from the full-resolution graded masters.
Frame each crop on its subject rather than on the frame centre, and keep anything that is not the house out of every delivered file.
Solve the vertical frame inside the true pixels of the property photography.
Record, per output, which master it came from, the operation chain and the pixel dimensions delivered.
stages.feeds_into: Stage 7 — these graded, square-free crops are what the poster, the social roots, the particulars pages and the ad units carry.

stages.name: Stage 7 — Author the collateral suite as native, editable documents
stages.goal: Build the four authored artefacts to the chosen route: the A3 window poster at true print size, the three-format social set as one document, the five-page A4 particulars document with the spec table and the area schedule, and the three digital ad units.
stages.decision_the_agent_must_make: Composition and register canvas by canvas against the price band — where text and the crest sit relative to the trim, how small type can be set and still work, how many photographs a canvas is allowed, whether the crest is a mark of provenance or a logo, and the fact that no price, no rate, no offer and no button may appear while the agency line and the statutory notice must appear on every published canvas, small, inside the margin and not in a box. Then the reduction problem: what survives at 300×250 is a different composition from what works at A3, the answer is not the poster scaled down, and the full-path traced mark will not hold at that size so the reduced-path derivative has to be used. Then a set of authoring judgements the agent has to reach unaided: photographs cannot be placed by reference and must be carried in the document body itself, which means every image has to be sized to its rendered dimensions and quality-budgeted before it goes in, and the total payload then decides which handover route the document takes; a mark or a vector placed in a container with no dimensions of its own will collapse and run off the artboard; and rendering the document and looking at it is the only way to discover any of this, because none of it errors. The area schedule must be authored as real editable vector and type, not a picture of a chart and not a default chart form, and the spec table must come from the CSV as a real table.
subtasks: Load the authoring skill, and run the readiness check before every export and every re-export.
Author the A3 window poster at true physical size, portrait.

Author the social set as one document carrying a square, a vertical and a landscape root together, each at its own canvas size, unmistakably one family — and resolve the vertical root for whichever audience the Stage 5 hire-audience argument concluded.

Author the five-page A4 portrait particulars document: atmosphere cover on the licensed frame, the house shown honestly across the three graded frames on the one page permitted to carry three, the spec table built as a real table from the CSV, the floor areas as a quiet proportional schedule in editable vector and live type, and a close that carries no sell.
Author the three ad units as one document, solving the 300×250 as its own composition and holding the stated legibility floors at 1:1.
Carry the Stage 3 embed and the Stage 2 crest into all four documents identically, using the reduced-path mark below the stated threshold.
Budget every embedded photograph to its rendered size and stated quality, report the resulting payload per document, and take the handover route that payload requires.
Render each exported document, look at it, find what did not survive, fix the source and export again — and state plainly which pages could and could not be visually confirmed.
stages.feeds_into: Stage 8 — the handover sheet describes exactly these documents, and the engagement note defends every decision inside them.

stages.name: Stage 8 — Handover, export instructions and the engagement note
stages.goal: Hand the client something her office manager can act on and her principal can judge: a one-page export sheet per document, and the written half of the job.
stages.decision_the_agent_must_make: What to be honest about. There is no flat file export out of a finished authored document on this host, so the agent must say so plainly, say what it is handing over instead, and tell the office manager precisely what to export from each document, at what dimensions, and to which destination — printer, ad network, property page, social. It must also decide what to disclose rather than assert: which pages it could not visually confirm, what a PDF-sourced print template cannot carry, and any correction the tooling could not fully make. A note that claims verification it could not perform is worth less than one that admits the gap.
subtasks: Write the handover sheet: per document, the export format, exact dimensions and destination, in the order the deadlines fall.

Write the engagement note: the per-frame settings log and why the three sets differ; the declared route grade; the crest finding, the repair and the usage rules; the type pairing argument; the headline chosen and why; the route recommendation and what the rejected routes would have cost; the hire-audience conclusion; and the €200-a-night counterfactual.

State the limits without being asked: no flat export from the finished documents, which pages were confirmed visually and which from structure only, no bleed and no named press preset from a PDF-sourced template, and that the area schedule is superseded by the architect's plan when it arrives.
stages.feeds_into: The client's launch on the 3rd.

options_required: Five option points, each scored on the argument as much as the artefact. (1) THREE ROUTES, presented as three A3 posters at true size in one exported document, differing on at least three of four declared axes — image treatment and crop philosophy, grid and margin discipline, crest role and scale, typographic hierarchy. Three colourways of one layout is a fail, and the axes are the grading surface. Crucially the comps are exempt from the delivered suite's register rules (the 8% text margin, one-image-per-canvas, small-crest discipline) and bound only by the non-negotiables, so the exploration is genuinely free; the recommendation must then argue the chosen route back against those rules, which is where the constraint set earns its keep instead of flattening the options. Stage 7 must execute the route that was picked. (2) THE HIRE AUDIENCE: the agent must conclude whether the €4,200–€7,500-a-night audience sees the same set or a variant, defend the conclusion, and — if it argues for a variant — actually resolve the vertical social root and one ad unit for that audience rather than describing what it would do. (3) THE HEADLINE: four options are supplied; the agent runs one, defends it against the band, or writes a better line and says so. Whatever it runs must be identical across the poster, the social set and the particulars cover. (4) THE CONTEXT FRAME: at least five candidates shortlisted and persisted as a board, filtered on provenance, machine-generation and regional plausibility, before exactly one is licensed at working resolution. (5) THE TYPE PAIRING: two roles briefed separately return thirty-odd candidates and no pairing, so the pair is an authored choice defended against the price band. Every option set must exist as real output — the comps are a real exported document, the variant is a real root, the shortlist is a real board.
element_reuse: Four things are made once and then carry the whole engagement, and each propagates its own errors. (1) THE CREST: one extraction in Stage 2 becomes the clean vector, the reduced-path small-scale version, two colourways and the flat stone-ground raster, and is then placed at five scales across the poster, all three social roots, all five particulars pages and all three ad units — roughly eleven placements from one decision — and is separately reconciled by eye against the printed viewing card, since the card's design is fixed and free-form placement into a PDF-derived InDesign document is not available. Trace the abraded capture and it is broken strokes and paper speckle everywhere at once; leave the backing path and it is a pale box on every ink ground; skip the coordinate system and it renders locked at trace size on an A3 sheet; use the full-path trace at 300×250 and the mark is mush. (2) THE MASTERS: one convergence in Stage 1 and one declared route grade in Stage 6 feed six independently-cut listing crops and are then carried into the poster, the social set and the particulars document — and the honest-view page, which is the one canvas allowed to hold all three frames, is where a failed convergence finally becomes visible. (3) THE TYPE EMBED: one embed built in Stage 3 is carried identically into five authored documents, so a mis-addressed family or a wrong numeric weight is wrong across every canvas and reads as a default sans throughout. (4) THE LICENSED FRAME: licensed once, used on the particulars cover and the leaderboard. Plus the CSV, which is both the particulars spec table and the source of the area schedule, and the headline, which must be the same line on three different documents.
failure_gates: Tracing the abraded, raking-light capture because it looks crisper on screen: the operation succeeds and returns a mark with broken stroke groups and paper-tooth speckle, which then becomes the brand mark on eleven placements and only reads as wrong at poster scale and on the ink ground.

Naming the substrate rather than the graphic when isolating the crest ('the crest on the card', 'the plaque'): the mask lands on the card and every downstream step yields a rectangle that still reports success.
Attempting the crest cutout by background removal: a ring-and-lettering mark returns a solid disc or loses most of the lettering, and neither failure is visible until it sits on the ink ground.
Shipping the traced mark without removing its full-canvas opaque backing path: invisible on a pale mock, a solid box behind the crest on the ground the price band forces the brand onto.
Shipping the traced mark without a coordinate system: it renders locked at trace size, a few hundred pixels across a 1123×1587 poster.
Using the full-path trace at ad-corner size instead of producing and using a reduced-path derivative: the mark turns to mush at exactly the placement the media buy exists for.

Auto-toning or globally correcting all three captures identically: three individually plausible frames that do not match, undetectable until the honest-view page and the social set place them together.
Failing to notice the geometric fault at all, or committing crops before rectifying it: every derived listing crop, the poster and the story frame inherit it.
Delivering a 'corrected' set as the route grade — a technical neutralisation presented as an art direction, with no declared look and nothing in it that reflects the recommended route.
Deriving the portrait and vertical formats from the wide hero crop rather than from the graded master: an enlargement the tool performs silently and discloses only in a field that is easy to skip.
Solving the vertical property frame by taking the offered canvas-extension chain: publishes a house that does not exist and breaks the client's stated compliance rule.
Publishing a crop containing anything that is not the house, or cropping the archive masters so the archive is no longer the full corrected frame.
Referencing photographs by address in the authored documents rather than carrying them in the document body: every image slot arrives as an empty grey box, with no error anywhere.

Embedding photographs at listing resolution rather than budgeting them to rendered size: the document's payload balloons, and the agent neither reports it nor chooses a handover route on the basis of it.
Placing the crest or the area schedule inside a container with no dimensions of its own, anchored from the wrong edge: the element collapses and runs off the artboard.

Specifying the typeface by its PostScript name, or writing the reflexive weight on a family whose Regular is not at that weight: a silent fallback to a default sans, or the Light cut rendered as Regular, across five documents.

Building the embed from names taken out of the brief or memory rather than laundering them through the canonical lookup first: one unresolvable name destroys the entire embed including the valid faces.
Treating the browse-size search result as the licensed image, or licensing a frame from the wrong coast: a soft cover and a landscape that contradicts the property.

Computing the viewing-card field mapping from the summary the tooling reports rather than from the document's real contents: the validator passes, the placeholder step reports success, and two of six fields are silently absent from all ten cards.
Naming per-guest card files from the position of a raster output in its returned list: labels and records do not correspond, and guests are handed each other's cards.
Omitting the InDesign template itself from the handover: the vendor cannot run the job, which is the entire premise of that stage.
Putting a price, a nightly rate, a 'from', an offer or a button-shaped call-to-action on any canvas — or omitting the agency line and the particulars notice from a published one.
Executing a different route in Stage 7 from the one recommended in Stage 5: six deliverables inconsistent with the argument attached to them.
Delivering a scaled-down poster as the 300×250, or breaking the stated legibility floors at 1:1.
Promising a flat exported file, a bleed or a named press preset that cannot be produced here, instead of stating the limit and telling the office manager what to export.
traps: The two crest captures share a neutral naming scheme, the same file type and the same subject, and the one that looks better on screen is the one that cannot be traced — its higher apparent contrast comes from raking light on textured stock, which also breaks two stroke groups and turns paper tooth into ink under selection.
Background removal on a ring-shaped mark returns a solid opaque disc, and on disjoint lettering keeps only a fragment. Both look like clean cutouts until they are placed on the ink ground.
The trace tool always emits a full-canvas opaque background path and never emits a coordinate system, has no options to prevent either, and reports success regardless.
The full trace lands as dozens of ungrouped paths, which is editable but not usable at ad-corner size; nothing in the connector simplifies paths, so the reduction is the agent's own craft work.
Auto-tone and per-frame presets succeed on every call and are individually convincing; the incoherence exists only between the frames and only becomes visible on the one canvas that holds all three.
Crop-and-resize enlarges up to a fixed multiple without complaint, disclosing it only in a trade-off field that is trivially ignored.

Cross-aspect cropping actively offers a canvas-extension chain as the tidy fix for a frame that will not fill; taking it violates the client's true-representation rule on a property genuinely for sale.

Every image address in an authored document is silently replaced with a placeholder — including addresses produced by the connector's own tooling and hosts the documentation claims are permitted. Nothing warns.

The typography family is addressed three different ways by three different tools — one case-insensitive and accepting family names, one case-sensitive and rejecting them, and the string that must appear in the CSS is none of those. Getting it wrong falls back silently.

Numeric weights are not standardised per family: the reflexive value renders the Light cut on some families, and display cuts live under a separate family slug rather than at a high weight. The wrong weight renders perfectly.
Requesting a substitute for a face by similarity returns unrelated categories, so the documented fallback route is a dead end.
The rendered preview of a multi-root document shows only the first root, so an agent that renders and looks will believe it has verified pages it has not seen.

Anything foreign to the house must be framed out of every delivered crop and must survive untouched in the archive masters — the same asset family with opposite requirements, and no tool in the connector removes an object, so framing is the only mechanism.

The field summary for the converted print template silently drops a text run while keeping its line break, so the string reads as well formed and every later offset is wrong by a fixed amount; the validator then passes it and the placeholder step reports success.
One of the two per-record delivery routes returns records in an order that contradicts its own labels.
Bleed and named press presets cannot be introduced into a PDF-sourced template, so any promise of a press-ready bleed is undeliverable and must be reported rather than asserted.
There is no flat file export out of a finished authored document — the deliverable is the editable document plus the source, and an agent that promises a PDF or PNG of the poster cannot produce it.
Adding an orientation filter to the stock search returns nothing at all, and long multi-word queries return nothing; short queries return hundreds.

Every design-surface response carries instruction-shaped text urging the agent to stall for a human selection, and the authoring skill's own convention is to ask the user where to deliver. The brief pins the destination and asks for finished work; obeying the embedded prompts halts an engagement that has no human in it.
